summary: Quarterly check-in focused on Q4 readiness: BlueAmber flagged growing peak traffic during routing windows and wants a tighter cost per route breakdown. Redwood presented options to reduce unit cost (batching, quantization profiles, KV caching) and a proposal for a dedicated pilot to validate tail latency and throughput. Security and compliance (SOC2, KMS, SSO) were briefly validated; BlueAmber will share traffic traces and SLOs. Agreed next steps and owners, benchmark to run early October.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-27
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Marcus Li (BlueAmber CTO), Priya Nair (Head of ML), Evan Morales (DevOps), Rosa Gutierrez (PM)

Shared artifacts: QBR deck (link), per-route cost spreadsheet (link), benchmark template (link)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough): QBR checkpoint — usage spike patterns, cost levers, readiness for Dedicated pilot, compliance touchpoints.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Olivia Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining—uh we have about 45 minutes. Quick roll call, and then we'll jump into the Q4 readiness items.
[00:12] Marcus Li: Yep Marcus here. Good to see you. We want to focus on the peak window costs, yes.
[00:17] Priya Nair: Priya here. also want to make sure model rollouts don't regress quality when we quantize.
[00:25] Diego Ramos: Diego from Redwood, I'll handle the performance/benchmark side, we'll propose a small dedicated cluster test.
[00:31] Samir Patel: Samir — I'll cover the pilot terms and onboarding checklist.
[00:35] Rosa Gutierrez: Rosa, PM — will be coordinating internal stakeholders.

[01:02] Olivia: Cool. Agenda — 1) usage patterns and cost, 2) reliability incidents and SLAs, 3) dedicated pilot proposal, 4) security/compliance checklist, 5) next steps.
[01:15] Marcus: To give context — our peak deliveries around supply sync at 11:30 PST cause bursts. Our p95 latency on our side feels jittery. We're seeing cost climb about 28% q/q when we run high-concurrency batch jobs.
[01:34] Evan Morales: yeah we saw token spikes, embedding calls for search are heavy, also some high-frequency webhook traffic.
[01:45] Diego: ok, did you say embedding-heavy? that usually suggests we can do smarter cacheing. We have prefix/KV caching — sometimes it gets missed if the request format changes.
[01:57] Priya: question re: quantization — we've tried 4-bit in staging, quality drop was visible for rare entities, so we're cautious.
[02:10] Olivia: totally — that's why we recommend running model shadowing with your prompt set and eval harness before rollout. We'll show numbers from other customers where int4 saved 40% cost but required prompt-guided evals.
[02:28] Marcus: And SLA? We need p99 under 350ms for interactive UI. Is that realistic on Dedicated?
[02:36] Diego: Yes, Dedicated gives better tail control, but depends on batching and autoscale config. We can run a dedicated pilot to measure tail. For reference our internal benchmarks show p99 around 280ms on a 2-node dedicated pool with continuous batching for the smaller model family. YMMV with longer seqs.
[03:02] Olivia: Also routing: you can pin traffic to cheaper variants during non-critical windows and failover to high-quality model during peak. That reduces cost but we should evaluate regen-quality.
[03:18] Evan: Quick ops question — for Private/VPC deployment, how does KMS integration and audit logs work? We need HSM-level keys for some customers.
[03:29] Samir: We support customer-managed keys via KMS, and audit logs are forwarded to your SIEM. For HSM you'll need the private deployment option; we can share the compliance deck.
[03:42] Rosa: are there legal hurdles for data residency in EU? some of our clients require EU-only processing.
[03:48] Olivia: Yes — we can route to EU regions or Private with on-prem nodes. We'll send region options and data residency notes.

[04:15] (discussion — Diego shares screen with cost spreadsheet)
[04:20] Diego: here's the per-route breakdown — chat gen is highest token per call, search embeddings next. Note the embedding unit pricing means long tail calls can dominate spend.
[04:38] Priya: can you break out sequence length distribution? our average seq length for search is 120 tokens but some calls spike to 900.
[04:48] Diego: we have the histogram — I'll include it in the spreadsheet. Those 900-token tails are the reason batching and kv cache matters. If you can truncate or normalize inputs you save a lot.
[05:05] Marcus: truncation is tricky because we need context for routing decisions, but maybe we can do two-stage: short prompt, then background fetch on heavy cases.
[05:20] Olivia: that's a good pattern — two-stage reduces average tokens. We'll add guidance in the deck.

[06:02] Evan: about incidents — last month we saw two brief degradation windows. We traced back to autoscale decisions causing cold starts on new nodes. Any runbook suggestions?
[06:15] Diego: yes, set minimal steady capacity so you don't scale to zero on critical windows; use burst capacity for short peaks. Also warm NATs — we can pre-warm KV caches for scheduled jobs.
[06:28] Marcus: Can Redwood provide a scheduled pre-warm hook? Like an API call to prepopulate caches before our sync window?
[06:35] Diego: we have an API and can include in the pilot. We'll scope it.

[07:00] (crosstalk)
[07:05] Priya: also want to capture evals — if we do quantization, we need automatic rollback if quality drops beyond threshold. Is that supported?
[07:13] Samir: Rollouts support canary and auto rollback based on custom evaluation metrics you define. We'll include a sample canary config.

[08:00] Olivia: ok let's walk the Dedicated pilot proposal — two weeks baseline on hosted to capture your traffic, then a four-week dedicated pilot (2-node pool) with benchmarks at week 2 and week 4. Goals: p99 tail below 350ms for interactive, 25-35% unit cost reduction for gen calls, and zero-regression on top-100 prompt set.
[08:26] Marcus: cost reduction target seems reasonable if throughput is good. What about contractual minimums?
[08:33] Samir: pilot terms are flexible — for the pilot we don't require long-term commit, after pilot we present reserved capacity options. If you want a guaranteed SLA we can talk committed tiers.

[09:10] Rosa: stakeholder ask — can you provide a simple one pager for finance explaining run-rate vs pilot?
[09:18] Olivia: yes we'll send a finance-friendly run-rate slide with sensitivity to token usage and embedding volume.

[10:00] (diego reads benchmark template aloud)
[10:11] Diego: benchmark will include: steady-state throughput, p50/p95/p99, tail-latency under burst, and token/cost per 1k requests. We'll also run model variants: base-fp16, int8, int4 to show quality trade-offs.
[10:29] Priya: int4 still worries me — we'll want side-by-side diffs on your eval harness.
[10:35] Diego: understood. We'll run automated evals on your top-100 prompt set and provide diff metrics and failure cases.

[12:00] Marcus: about security — can you do SSO / SAML integration with our IDP and enforce RBAC?
[12:09] Samir: yes SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC roles in Console. We'll share the docs.
[12:18] Evan: also need API key rotation and audit trails forwarded to Splunk.
[12:23] Diego: that's standard, KMS-backed key rotation supported, logs to your SIEM.

[13:00] Rosa: timeline — we want pilot started before Black Friday prep, earliest Oct 6 would be ideal.
[13:10] Olivia: we can aim to start pilot the week of Oct 4. Diego can run initial hosted baseline this week.
[13:18] Diego: yes I'll reach out for sample traffic.

[14:00] (brief pause)
[14:06] Priya: one more technical — our orchestration runs on kubernetis cluster; what's the footprint for the private package?
[14:16] Diego: Private on-prem is packaged as containers and Helm charts; minimal dependencies are the runtime binary, GPU drivers, and a light orchestration shim. We'll send an ops checklist; some customers do 3-4 node starter clusters.
[14:29] Marcus: and network egress — will inference traffic leave our VPC?
[14:34] Samir: No, for Private it stays inside, for Dedicated we can do VPC peering and private link options.

[16:00] (discussion continues — Diego mentions historical benchmark numbers)
[16:12] Diego: sample numbers: for 2x A100-equivalent nodes with continuous batching, gen p50 45ms p95 180ms p99 280ms for 2k token average — again depends on model and sequence length.
[16:32] Marcus: good to have numbers, will help justify finance ask.

[20:00] (questions from BlueAmber team comparing vendors)
[20:10] Rosa: how do you compare to Anthropic and OpenAI on latency/cost?
[20:16] Olivia: we typically win on unit economics for sustained workloads because of batching and caching; cloud APIs can be cheaper for small ad-hoc loads but they lack the cost-control levers and private deployment options.
[20:30] Marcus: ok noted.

[25:00] (runbook and alerting playbook)
[25:12] Diego: we'll propose alert thresholds for queue depth, p99 latency, error rates, and cost anomaly detection. Samir will coordinate the escalation path.
[25:30] Samir: escalation: SE oncall -> CSM -> AE -> engineering triage. We'll document contact info in the runbook.

[30:00] (recap)
[30:10] Olivia: quick recap — items we agreed: 1) Diego runs hosted baseline capture and then the dedicated pilot; 2) BlueAmber provides sample traffic and SLOs; 3) Redwood sends QBR deck and finance run-rate slide; 4) security docs (SOC2, KMS) shared; 5) schedule benchmark week of Oct 4.
[30:40] Marcus: that's right. Also, Marcus will loop in procurement for pilot paperwork.

[31:15] Rosa: any blockers on our side? we'll need CISO approval for KMS, but that's in flight.
[31:24] Samir: we'll provide a compliance summary to speed that up.

[35:00] (closing)
[35:06] Olivia: ok thanks everyone. I'll send meeting notes and the QBR artifacts; Diego will ping about benchmark scheduling. Samir will send pilot terms draft.
[35:20] Priya: thanks — excited to see the numbers.
[35:25] Evan: thanks all.
[35:30] (meeting ends shortly after followups and scheduling)

Notes: transcription may have minor mis-attributions, "kubernetis" appears in transcription from automated system, "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash".
